# `set_stack_type`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Select the frame type that the stacker accumulates (light, dark, bias or flat) and, for flat, an auto-exposure flag.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe7250, SetStackType @0x1927d0 (64-bit build) |

Stores the frame type and auto-exposure flag. Changing away from an existing calibration type clears the stack and the calibration frame and count caches, or restores the light-stack counts; selecting the type already in force is not refused by the type logic, but the call is refused while the Stack function is running, even for the same type. No camera-open or mount check is made and no worker is started. There are no numeric exposure, limit or count inputs. The clearing step takes locks without a bounded timeout.

Side effects: Stores the frame type and flat auto-exposure flag; may clear the accumulated stack and calibration caches or restore light-stack counts.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_stack_type"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Parameters of set_stack_type. The device also accepts the positional form [type, autoexp] (first two array elements); other object keys are ignored. [READ] |
| `params.type` | string | yes | - | Frame type to stack: light, dark, bias or flat, matched case-insensitively and exactly. An empty or unrecognised name is rejected with 209. 'unknown' is not accepted. [READ] |
| `params.autoexp` | boolean | no | false | Auto-exposure flag. Parsed only when type is flat; accepts a JSON boolean or integer (zero is false, non-zero true). A present value of any other type is rejected with 106 when type is flat, and silently ignored for light, dark and bias. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | type missing or not a string (also params absent, null, scalar, wrong top-level shape or empty array) | `expected string param` |
| 209 | type is empty or not one of light, dark, bias, flat | `invalid value` |
| 106 | type is flat and autoexp is present with a type other than boolean or integer | `expected bool param` |
| 259 | The Stack function is running | `stack is already running` |
| 204 | Internal frame-type value above 3; not reachable from validated handler input | `out of limit` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, light:

```json
{"id":31,"method":"set_stack_type","params":{"type":"light"}}
```

Request, flat-autoexp:

```json
{"id":32,"method":"set_stack_type","params":{"type":"flat","autoexp":true}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_stack_type","result":0,"code":0,"id":31}
```

Reply, stack-running:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_stack_type","error":"stack is already running","code":259,"id":33}
```
